anchors.title: Medium multi-crate inner-loop workspace on Linux

representative_shape.target_posture: single dominant host target with optional nightly comparison

required_traits: more than one crate participates in normal edit/build/test flow
at least one repeated inner-loop operation is expensive enough to diagnose
build or timing receipts can be recorded or imported
the case includes both local and CI-adjacent decision pressure
hold_constant: artifact collection posture across compared runs
allowed_variation: presence of rust-analyzer or editor-adjacent consumers
exact build-analysis or timing attachment family
notes: This anchor is for comparability of inner-loop decisions, not leaderboard-grade benchmarking.
A tiny one-crate demo does not satisfy this anchor.

anchors.title: Publishable library family at release boundary

representative_shape.workspace_shape: publishable library or small library family
representative_shape.target_posture: stable release path with docs.rs relevance when applicable

required_traits: there is a meaningful public surface or declared boundary under review
release, migration, or semver-related decisions are in scope
docs or semantic imports are available or explicitly absent with reason
allowed_variation: whether docs.rs or local rustdoc JSON is used
notes: A library-only note with no stated public-boundary posture does not satisfy this anchor.
This anchor is about release-boundary comparison, not generic code quality.

anchors.title: Restricted consumer with explicit intake controls

representative_shape.workspace_shape: consumer workspace with package intake controls
representative_shape.target_posture: stable install/build path after explicit review

required_traits: route or source authority matters before use
payload staging or extraction assumptions matter
hold_constant: package identity and intake decision class
allowed_variation: registry vs mirror vs vendored route family
notes: Starting after bytes are already trusted does not satisfy this anchor.
This anchor is for intake posture, not all supply-chain questions at once.

anchors.title: Polyglot Rust/native component boundary
required_traits: there is an actual Rust/native or Rust/foreign-build boundary
provider, linker, build-script, or generated-binding posture matters
the comparison surfaces boundary-review or handoff decisions
allowed_variation: specific foreign language or build tool
which boundary attachment family is emitted
notes: A pure-Rust workspace with no foreign-build or ABI surface does not satisfy this anchor.
This anchor compares specialist boundary truth, not generic portability.

anchors.title: Docs-derived routed support case with cross-target drift risk

representative_shape.environment: docs generation or docs-adjacent consumer routing
representative_shape.target_posture: docs.rs default target plus at least one local target when relevant

required_traits: claims are derived from docs, rustdoc JSON, or routed consumer slices
target or environment assumptions can drift
the pilot leaves behind an explicitly lossy consumer handoff where needed
hold_constant: declared consumer class or routed brief class
primary docs or semantic import lane
notes: A docs-derived claim with no stated target posture does not satisfy this anchor.
This anchor is about support and routing drift, not all documentation quality questions.
